comments.content:
By "manually" it is meant to set priviliges via supabase's dashboard UI, right?
As far as I remember https://audit.ubq.fi/ needs access only to the `permits` table so it seems to be ok to allow https://audit.ubq.fi/ read access to the `permits` table.

The best thing we can do in this case is to describe the required RLS/CLS setup in the README file
Yes
Yes, migrations in the current repo are deprecated. Migrations for the [kernel](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel) are not yet created and I'm in doubt if we need ones since all of the kernel plugins will have their own DBs so I'm not sure what exactly we need to store in the kernel's DB.

Right now we're using a pavlovcik's supabase DB instance with disabled [RLS](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/row-level-security)
What should be done:
1. Make sure that [RLS](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/row-level-security) is enabled and the bot acts as expected
2. Enable [CLS](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/column-level-security) and make sure that `permits.transaction` field can only be updated by an authorized user who matches `permits.beneficiary_id` (related [comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/pull/173#discussion_r1502727455))
